title.narrative: Saksham - Empowering Youth with Skills for a Brighter Future

description.narrative: Marginalized NEET youth aged 18–24 in Delhi NCR and 18–35 in Bikaner (Rajasthan), face barriers to sustainable livelihood opportunities, due to gender inequalities and gaps in skills, training access and employment opportunities. Root cause analysis: The labour market challenges in Rajasthan, particularly in Bikaner, are driven by interconnected structural, institutional, and skills-related factors that continue to constrain youth employability. Formal skilling systems demonstrate significant delivery gaps, with 42.8% under DDUGKY and 96.9% under MMMSY, indicating a mismatch between skilling provision and labour market requirements. These gaps reflect limited access to demand-driven, localized, and outcome-oriented training that responds to market needs and evolving economic opportunities. Women face additional structural barriers that further limit their participation in the labour market. Social norms, safety concerns and limited access to skills continue to restrict female mobility and participation. As a result, many young women remain concentrated in low-paid occupations with limited opportunities for career progression and economic empowerment. Digital readiness also remains a significant constraint. The 40–45% shortfall in job-ready youth for ITeS/BPO roles reflects gaps in digital and financial literacy, communication skills, and familiarity with artificial intelligence (AI) tools. While access to mobile phones has increased, many young people lack the digital and workplace competencies required for entry-level jobs in the emerging market economy. At the same time, first-generation job seekers continue to encounter systemic barriers in transitioning from education to employment. Rajasthan’s 28.5% unemployment rate and over 55% joblessness among educated youth highlight weak school-to-work transition mechanisms, inadequate career guidance, limited employer engagement, and no workplace exposure. These factors reduce employability, restrict access to sustainable livelihood opportunities.

Project Saksham will implement activities across outreach, training, social and gender skills, financial literacy, employment, self-employment, employer and educational institution engagement, and alumni development. Activities will be implemented across Delhi NCR and Bikaner, Rajasthan during the project period, with progress tracked through project MIS, participant records, progress reports, training assessments and follow-up. 1. Mobilization, Awareness and Enrolment The project will conduct 45 awareness events through community meetings, campaigns, schools, information kiosks, social media and brochures to identify and reach potential participants. Training centres will be set up with the required infrastructure, teaching-learning material and practical labs. Youth will undergo basic aptitude, communication and screening before enrolment. The project will enrol 1,500 youth (900 female and 600 male) and maintain participant-level records through the project MIS. 2. Market-Aligned Vocational Skills Training Enrolled youth will receive market-aligned Vocational Skills Training through wage-employment-oriented and self-employment-oriented pathways. Domain Skill Training will cover sectors such as BFSI, Retail, ITeS and Entrepreneurship. The project will support completion of training by 998 youth in wage-employment-oriented training and 428 youth in self-employment-oriented training, with participant lists and attendance records maintained as evidence. Training will also include Digital Skills Training, IT and AI sessions, financial literacy, gender and life-skills. These components will be delivered alongside domain skills to support the development of social and economic skills for wage or self-employment. 3. Social Skills and Gender Training The project will organise aligned social skills and gender training for 1,500 young women and men, with 60% women and young girls. The activity will also engage the wider stakeholders identified in the LFA: 1,500 parents, 50 private sector employers and 50 community leaders/opinion makers. Ten vocational trainers—five female and five male—will receive ToT training. Employer and community-level sessions will address gender mainstreaming, gender equality, safety and security. 4. Financial Literacy and Access to Financial Services Financial literacy training will be provided to 1,500 youth, including 900 female and 600 male participants. The project will support all 1,500 young women and men to have operational bank accounts and record this through project MIS data. The activity will provide the financial literacy component required under the LFA and establish the basis for participants to access financial services. 5. Industry Engagement and Wage Employment The project will organise 5 career fairs, including 5 rural and 5 urban as specified in the LFA, and provide job mentoring on professional and personal needs to 1,500 young women and men. It will facilitate 50 on-the-job-trainings (OJTs) and 50 industry visits, supported by industry sessions and exposure activities. Job fairs, interview/placement drives, job and business development fairs and campus placements will be used to connect trained youth with employment opportunities. The employment activities will contribute to the LFA target of at least 1,125 (75%) JOVT and VTEP graduates placed into decent work within 3 months after graduation. 6. Self-Employment and Livelihood Linkages For youth pursuing self-employment, the project will provide business development training and support participants to develop 300 business plans. A total of 225 youth—135 female and 90 male—will be linked to aligned youth and gender-friendly financial services, while 225 trainees—135 female and 90 male—will receive business mentoring on professional and personal needs. These activities will provide the defined pathway from training to self-employment and entrepreneurship. 7. Employer and Educational Institution Engagement The project will engage 40 employers through sensitization/training on gender equality, including gender wage parity, statutory laws, safety and security at the workplace. It will identify 10 good practices among private sector stakeholders in gender-transformative youth employment under decent conditions and engage 10 educational institutions—schools, colleges and universities—to strengthen delivery of market-aligned digital, vocational and entrepreneurial skills and sustained job placements. 8. Post-Placement Support, Job Retention and Business Mentoring Following placement or transition to self-employment, the project will provide post-placement support, job retention and business mentoring during the first six months. Support will include mentoring on professional and personal needs, collection and use of employer and trainee feedback, and follow-up on transition into jobs and self-employment opportunities. The activity will track employment and self-employment outcomes through project MIS and follow-up mechanisms.

Project Saksham, Plan India’s flagship skilling initiative since 2010, have equipped more than 200,000 disadvantaged youth with market-oriented vocational and life skills. Over 60% of graduates have been young women, with a 70% placement/self-employment success rate and employment. This project builds on established infrastructure, while expanding to underserved communities in Delhi NCR and Bikaner, introducing AI-enabled digital skills, institutional linkages and alumni career progression. The project is aligned with Plan Global Strategy and Plan India’s national goals. The intervention complements government and market-led efforts, including RSLDC, DDUGKY and MMYSY, alongside NSDC and Sector Skill Councils for standardized curriculum and certification. NGOs and private providers offer localized employability training, while MFIs and SHGs facilitate credit for women’s enterprises. However, gaps persist in localized training access, particularly in Bikaner; digital and AI readiness; gender-responsive participation and retention; and sustained career progression. Saksham addresses these through community-based JOVT/VTEP centres, AI-integrated training, gender-transformative engagement, corporate placement pipelines, microfinance linkages, six-month mentoring and leadership pathways for 150 alumni.

SUMMARY - SAKSHAM - Empowering Youth with Skills for a Brighter Future is a three-year initiative by Plan India that supports disadvantaged youth, especially young women, through market-oriented vocational training, digital and AI skills, life skills, financial literacy, and pathways to employment or entrepreneurship. The project targets Delhi NCR and Bikaner, where young people face high unemployment, limited access to relevant training, gender-related barriers, and a widening digital divide. Saksham aims to train 1,500 young people, at least 60% of whom will be young women, and help them access decent work or self-employment through training, employer partnerships, job placement, entrepreneurship support, and post-placement mentoring.

Saksham incorporates sustainability measures across the Financial, Institutional, Environmental, Technical and Social (FIETS) dimensions to sustain employment, self-employment and livelihood outcomes beyond the project period. Financial Sustainability: The intervention will strengthen financial sustainability by establishing linkages with government schemes, forge employer partnerships, and linkages with financial institutions for funding opportunities. Support for wage employment, entrepreneurship, and access to financial services enhances income generation for beneficiaries, while partnerships with training institutions, employers, and local stakeholders help sustain skilling and employment pathways beyond the project period. Institutional Sustainability: The intervention will strengthen the capacity of training centres, employers, community stakeholders, alumni groups, through standardized training systems, industry partnerships, and collaborative engagement. Strengthened institutional linkages, employer networks, and alumni engagement will support continued skilling, placement, mentoring, and knowledge sharing, enabling sustainable employment pathways beyond the project period. Technical Sustainability: The intervention will equip centres with relevant training resources that can continue to be used beyond the project period. Training materials, and established maintenance and asset management practices enable continued delivery of quality skilling programmes after project completion. Environmental Sustainability: The intervention will minimize its environmental footprint by promoting digital learning resources, responsible use of training materials, and resource-efficient operations. It will also prepare young people on environmental awareness and sustainable workplace practices, while encouraging green behaviours and considering climate-related risks in programme implementation wherever relevant. Social Sustainability: The intervention will promote inclusion by prioritizing disadvantaged youth, particularly young women and first-generation job seekers, NEET, through accessible training, community mobilisation, and training. Continued linkages with employers, government schemes and services, alumni group will help sustain access to skilling and livelihood opportunities beyond the project period.

The project aims to enable marginalized NEET youth to access and sustain employment and livelihood opportunities in the target areas of Delhi NCR and Bikaner, by addressing skills mismatch, limited access to market-aligned training, gaps in digital and financial skills, gender-related barriers, and establish linkages with sustainable livelihood opportunities. The change process combines community mobilisation, market-aligned vocational training, digital and workplace skills, and employer partnerships to strengthen youth employability. Placement and entrepreneurship support, mentoring, and service linkages facilitate transitions to wage and self-employment. Post-placement support and alumni networks promote job retention and career progression. If disadvantaged youth, particularly young women and first-generation job seekers, receive market-aligned TVET training, digital and AI-enabled skills, life skills, and livelihood linkages, while employers, families, communities, alumni and government stakeholders remain key actors in the change process, Then youth will acquire market-relevant competencies, improve their employability and entrepreneurship capabilities, access to decent employment, and sustain their participation in the labour market. Because the intervention addresses the key barriers to employment—skills mismatch, structural barriers to women’s participation, digital competency gaps, and weak workplace transition, through an integrated ecosystem that connects training with employment opportunities.

The project will focus on disadvantaged youth aged 18–24 years in Delhi NCR and Bikaner, Rajasthan, particularly young women, who are NEET and face barriers to skills, employment and economic opportunities. Up to 35 years for self-employment/VTEP pathways. At least 60% of beneficiaries will be girls/young women.
